headline: Honesty is alignment between reality and what you say—the foundation of trust and effective action
universal_truth: Lies compound; every falsehood requires more falsehoods to maintain, while truth is stable
fun_facts: The average person hears 10-200 lies per day, from white lies to serious deception
Lying activates stress responses—polygraphs detect this physiological discomfort
Research shows honest people are perceived as more competent, not just more moral
discussion_questions: When is honesty difficult for you?
What's the difference between honesty and brutal honesty?
How does dishonesty affect relationships over time?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every lie creates a parallel reality that must be maintained—remembering what you said, to whom, keeping stories straight. Truth is simpler: reality is the record. Honesty isn't just moral; it's practical.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Everyone agrees honesty is important, yet everyone sometimes lies. When is honesty truly essential, and what makes it so hard to maintain?

options.text: Honesty often has short-term costs—discomfort, conflict, vulnerability—even when it has long-term benefits
options.response: Yes. Lies offer immediate relief while truth offers lasting stability. We trade future trust for present comfort. The math works short-term but fails long-term.

options.text: Some truths are harmful and kindness requires softening them
options.response: Kindness matters, but there's a difference between tact and deception...

q1.title: Lies Compound
q1.script: One lie requires another to support it. Details must be remembered, stories kept consistent. Lies are expensive—they demand ongoing cognitive maintenance. Truth, once told, needs no support. It aligns with reality.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Lies Compound"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trust Foundation
q2.script: Relationships run on trust, and trust requires honesty. A discovered lie doesn't just damage that statement—it casts doubt on everything. Once someone lies to you, you question what else isn't true.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Self-Deception
q3.script: The most dangerous lies are the ones we tell ourselves. Pretending we're fine when we're not. Ignoring problems that need addressing. Honesty with yourself is the hardest and most important kind.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Lies compound. Every falsehood requires more falsehoods to maintain, while truth is stable. Choose the harder short-term path for the easier long-term life.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 193. Tomorrow, we'll explore being the same when no one's looking—integrity. Until then, notice when you're tempted to shade the truth and ask: is this worth the cost?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Truth Check - Are You Honest with Yourself?
growTrack.activity: Consider one area where you might not be fully honest with yourself. A problem you're ignoring? A truth you're avoiding? Self-deception is the most expensive lie. What would change if you faced it honestly?
